requirements.rationale: F1049: six Opus mender turns in one night, each finding a review that was about to start. The author's run ending is what makes the work reviewable and already requests the next firing (`flow_advance.after_run`), so this is the flow working, not a stall.
requirements.statement: A flow firing that finds a `completed` task whose completing agent still has a run `running` on that task records no `loop_stalled` stall, briefs no mender, writes no `skipped` job run, and its decision carries no stall reason, whether or not other tasks of the flow are gated on that task's approval.

requirements.rationale: Requirement hand-off-gap-is-not-a-stall is safe only because this firing exists; the acceptance drive asserts both halves so neither can regress alone.
requirements.statement: When the completing agent's run on that task ends, the firing its end requests selects the task for review by a reviewer other than its author, without waiting for the flow's cron tick.

requirements.rationale: The fix narrows what counts as a stall; it must not delay a real one.
requirements.statement: A flow firing that finds open work, nothing claimable, and no agent's run `running` on any of the flow's tasks records a `loop_stalled` stall on that first firing and wakes the enabled mender once, as today.

requirements.rationale: Treating the task as in flight removes the firing's stall; the sweep is what keeps a run that never ends from hiding forever.
requirements.statement: A completed task held in flight by its author's run is still reported by the stall sweep when that run is recorded `running` but this Hub is not executing it (`dead_run`), and when its loop has had no run started and no task moved for `NO_PROGRESS_MINUTES` (`no_progress`).

requirements.rationale: On :8000 the operator chose a runner, not a model, and got Opus for 42 turns. Mending is reading state and calling a few routes; the everyday model is enough, and an operator who wants more can choose it.
requirements.statement: When the project's Manager mender entry names no model, every mender turn runs on the model the model catalog marks `default` for the CLI of the entry's runner (`claude-sonnet-5-5` for Claude Code), whatever model that runner itself names; a project whose entry already names no model moves to it at the mender's next wake, with no migration.
A model the operator chose for the mender on the Manager page is the model its turns run on, as today.

requirements.rationale: Warn, don't gate: the operator must be able to see what the mender costs before it runs.
requirements.statement: The Manager page's model menu for the mender, with no model chosen, names the model the mender will run on (for a Claude Code runner: 'Sonnet 5.5 (the mender's default)'), never 'The runner's model'; the other jobs' menus are unchanged.

requirements.rationale: 27 four-minute waits ran out unanswered on 2026-10-26/27. A wait on a person who is asleep only ends in 'nobody responded'.
requirements.statement: Every question the Hub's mender asks through `ask_user` is recorded with `blocking` false and no `wait_expires_at`, whatever `blocking` value it passed; the call returns without waiting; it parks no task; and a blocking question from any other agent still waits as today.

requirements.rationale: Keeps the rule that the hardcore moves wait for the operator, without a wait; F1048's rule then keeps the stall the operator's while its reason holds, so the note is not asked again.
requirements.statement: The mender's brief tells it that, for each action it must ask the operator about, it leaves the question as a note, does not take the action, and ends the stall with `mend_end_stall(stall_id, "gave_up", summary)` whose summary names the note.

requirements.rationale: The mender holds one open conversation per stall; delivering into the latest open one (`questions.py:164`) would wake it in another stall's thread.
requirements.statement: Answering (or declining) a question that no run is waiting on delivers the answer as a new queued turn into the conversation the question was asked from when that conversation is still open, and into the asker's latest open conversation only when it is not.

requirements.rationale: Today every non-blocking question whose run ended reads 'nobody is waiting on this answer any more' (`OverviewScreen.tsx:117`), which is false for a note whose answer is delivered.
requirements.statement: The Overview's Needs-you list shows each unanswered mender note with its question, an action that opens the conversation it was asked in, and no sentence saying nobody is waiting on the answer; the 'nobody is waiting' sentence is shown only for a blocking question whose asking turn has ended.
